key_insight: The study constructs a non-Gaussian, distribution-valued solution to the critical two-dimensional KPZ equation.
engineering_relevance: The result advances mathematical foundations for stochastic interface-growth models, rather than directly demonstrating AI-driven materials discovery.
method: Take critical scaling limits of centred log partition functions for 2D Gaussian directed polymers.
Apply a renormalised Cole–Hopf transformation to spatially mollified Critical 2D Stochastic Heat Flow.
Characterise covariance singularities and Gaussian fluctuations under shrinking-scale spatial averaging.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical construction and fluctuation results, including log-log covariance blow-up, but provides no experimental data or numerical benchmarks.
watch_item: The solution is distribution-valued; practical simulation methods and materials-specific validation are not established in the abstract.
